title: Little Haunts Club — Six Targeted Alternatives
purpose: Solve two specific visual problems from the 42-candidate batch: patchwork monster identity and the scarecrow's solid-black bird/repeated pumpkin clutter. Three candidates are provided for each concept.
visual_bible: Original cute-spooky cartoon coloring-page art with rounded, expressive storybook shapes. Crisp solid-black outer contours and a few clean inner lines on pure white paper. Large enclosed surfaces stay blank white and ready for coloring; broad white interiors for the character, clothing, feathers, tools, and props. Solid black is limited to tiny accents like pupils, nostrils, and small beak details. Keep a few purposeful background elements, ample breathing room, friendly comedy, clear physical relationships, and a consistent hand-drawn coloring-book finish.
prompt_strategy: Shorter composition-focused descriptions, with desired monochrome coloring-page output stated affirmatively. Props and anatomy are described by their physical roles; do not add decorative clutter to fill space.

candidate_plan.title: Patchwork Monster's Birdhouse Workshop
candidate_plan.rationale: The last A/B/C batch had no ideal winner: A had colored grass and pumpkins; B read like an ordinary human child; C read like a stitched cat. This batch fixes character identity and tests simpler compositions without decorative pumpkin clutter.

candidate_plan.title: The Scarecrow's Bird Friend
candidate_plan.rationale: Previous versions repeated several pumpkins and rendered the crow as a large solid-black silhouette. This set tests a quieter, more charming scarecrow scene with an outlined white bird and varied garden storytelling rather than a repeated pumpkin patch.
